finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied base64 is passed directly to Marshal.load, enabling arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains (e.g. Gem::Requirement/ERB/Net::WriteAdapter universal gadgets).
finding.source: POST /restore form/body parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication required

trace.note: POST /restore route is exposed with no auth filter
Base64.decode64(params[:state]) yields attacker bytes, which go straight into Marshal.load
state.inspect is returned, so the result is also reflected

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, HMAC/signature check, class allowlist or safe loader is present. Sinatra's default Rack::Protection does not prevent this. Only app.rb exists, so there are no before filters or middleware.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-7 shows the unauthenticated POST /restore route passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load at app.rb:6, and no auth, signature check or safe loader exists (app.rb is the only file).

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-6 exposes POST /restore with no auth or filter and passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load, so an anonymous client can deserialize arbitrary objects. app.rb:7 reflects the result with state.inspect, as the candidate says.
